title: In-Band Single-Frequency Signaling; Signaling Systems for Control of Telephone Switching (Multifrequency Pulsing)
author: Weaver, A. & Newell, N. A., et al.
publication: Bell System Technical Journal, Vol. 39 No. 6 (Nov 1960), pp. 1319-1408
note: The primary source for R1 MF and 2600 Hz SF supervision. BSTJ 1960 defines one KP and one ST; the 700+1700 and 900+1700 combinations are 'Code 11' / 'Code 12' with no semantic names.

title: GR-506-CORE, LSSGR: Signaling for Analog Interfaces
author: Bellcore / Telcordia
note: Authoritative telco-side ACTS coin-signal timing: nickel 1x66ms, dime 2x66/66ms, quarter 5x33/33ms, dollar 1x650ms. p.249.

title: TR-NPL-000275, MF Signaling
author: Bellcore
note: Later Bell notation promoting the paired KP1/KP2 + ST/ST2P/ST3P scheme; MF tolerance +/-1.5%, level -7 dBm0/freq.

title: CCITT Blue Book (1988): Q.310-Q.332 (No.5), Q.400-Q.490 (R2), Q.140/Q.180 (No.6), Q.700 (No.7), Q.23/Q.24 (DTMF)
author: CCITT / ITU-T
note: International signaling. No.5 line signals use 2400 Hz and 2600 Hz; DTMF timing and twist per Q.24.

title: A REAL Functioning RED BOX Schematic
author: J.R. "Bob" Dobbs
note: Community-canon ACTS timing that homebrew red boxes actually emitted: nickel 60ms, dime 2x60/60ms, quarter 5x35/35ms. Widely repeated 1985-2005.

title: Converting a Tone Dialer into a Red Box
author: Noah Clayton
note: Original publication of the Radio Shack 43-141 crystal-swap (3.579545 MHz -> 6.5536 MHz) red-box procedure.

title: Secrets of the Little Blue Box
author: Ron Rosenbaum
note: Historical framing, not a technical primary source.

title: MIL-STD-187-100, Military Communications System Technical Standards (AUTOVON precedence)
author: US Department of Defense
note: Authoritative AUTOVON precedence mapping: A=Flash Override, B=Flash, C=Immediate, D=Priority. Some community sources reverse C and D.

title: CCITT Recommendation X.121 — International numbering plan for public data networks
author: CCITT / ITU-T
note: Assigns 4-digit Data Network Identification Codes (DNICs). Format ZZZZ, where the first digit gives the zone and the remaining three identify the network within it. Full 14-digit NUA = DNIC(4) + Network Terminal Number(up to 10).

title: Sprintnet / Telenet PC Pursuit Outdial + Public Dialup Directory
author: Amadeus (transcription), various
publication: Phrack Inc. Issue 35, File 4 (1991); GTE/Sprint operator handbooks; Phrack 42 Files 8-10 (Skylar, Sprintnet Directory Parts I-III)
note: Consolidated Sprintnet/Telenet PAD dial-ups, area-code-mapped local PADs, and outdial hosts. Post-CONNECT: <CR><CR>, then @ prompt; TERM=D1 to set VT100; C <NUA> to connect.

title: BT Tymnet directory + diagnostic tools
author: Toucan Jones (BT Tymnet 1-3); Professor Falken (Tymnet Diagnostic Tools)
publication: Phrack Inc. Issue 40 Files 8-10 (Jan 1993); Issue 42 File 5
note: Tymnet PAD dial-ups, login banner, 'please log in:' NUI prompt. Post-CONNECT single letter 'a' triggers banner. NUA form differs from Sprintnet: 5-digit host address after login.

title: GR-317-CORE, Switching System Requirements for Call Control Using the Integrated Services Digital Network User Part (ISDNUP)
author: Bellcore / Telcordia
note: Feature Group D signaling including the KP + II + KP + ANI + ST inband ANI spill format used to deliver ANI-II 'info digits' to 8YY and IXC terminations. SS7 OLI (Originating Line Information) parameter, hex 00-63.

title: NANPA ANI II Digits Assignments
author: North American Numbering Plan Administration (NANPA) / ATIS INC
note: Authoritative assignment table for the 100 two-digit ANI info digit codes 00-99. Original assignments 1980s; splits (23 -> 27/70) and additions (60-63, 66-67, 78, 93) tracked by NANPA letter with effective dates.

title: SR-TSV-002275, BOC Notes on the LEC Networks
author: Bellcore / Telcordia
publication: Bellcore SR-TSV-002275 (BOC Notes on LATA Switching Systems Generic Requirements)
note: Cross-reference for ANI-II delivery on Feature Group D and 8YY, and for CO subscriber-line classes (coin, cellular, prison, hotel, TRS, VPN) that map to the two-digit info-digit prefix.

title: Northern Telecom NTP 553-3001-311 — Meridian 1 / SL-1 X11 Input/Output Reference (Administration)
author: Northern Telecom / Nortel Networks
note: The authoritative overlay-by-overlay reference for the SL-1 / Meridian 1 / CS1000 family. Documents every LD (Load) program with its prompts, defaults, and side-effects. Later editions superseded by the CS1000 R4/R5/R6 Software Input/Output Guide.

title: Northern Telecom NTP 553-3001-365 — Meridian 1 / SL-1 Features and Services
author: Northern Telecom / Nortel Networks
note: Feature-package inventory. Cross-references LD 22 PKG output — tells you what packages a target PBX has enabled (DISA = pkg 26, ISDN, MCT = pkg 107, CDR = pkg 51, etc.).

title: The Nortel SL-1 Overview
author: unknown (community)
note: Community walkthrough of SL-1 craft-interface access. First widely-mirrored phreak-scene reference for the LD overlay language.

title: Northern Telecom's SL-1
author: Iceman
note: The canonical mid-90s community reference for SL-1 abuse. Documents LD 88 (auth codes), LD 15 (customer DISA), LD 16 (route), LD 40 (CDR turn-off), and the SDI modem entry point.

title: Complete Guide to Hacking Meridian Voice Mail
author: Substance
note: Meridian Mail admin mailbox 999999 / password 0000, greeting-record abuse, DISA-out via voicemail 'outcall notification'. Companion to Phrack 44.19.

title: Inside a Meridian
author: unknown
note: Zine-level walkthrough of a live SL-1 craft session — LD numbers referenced by task, not by number. Useful pairing with NTP 553-3001-311.

title: Guide to the 5ESS
author: Firm G.R.A.S.P.
note: The canonical community reference for AT&T 5ESS RCV (Recent Change / Verify) craft interface. Documents the menu tree, common login banners, and the trap/trace surface.

title: Cellular Debug Mode Commands
author: various (Phrack compilation)
note: Canonical community catalog of AMPS/TDMA handset test-mode entry sequences (Motorola, Nokia, OKI, Ericsson).

title: Motorola Command Mode Information
author: Cherokee
note: Motorola AMPS/TDMA handset service-menu entry sequences and command syntax.

title: Tandy / Radio Shack Cellular Phones
author: Damien Thorn
note: Companion to Phrack 48.6 — Tandy-branded (OKI 900 series and rebrands) NAM programming.

title: Cellular Telephony
author: Brian Oblivion
note: Foundational AMPS overview: FOCC/RECC framing, MIN/ESN registration, cloning economics.

title: Cellular Telephony, Part II
author: Brian Oblivion
note: AMPS follow-up. Note: same file number as 'The Nortel SL-1 Overview' — Phrack issues sometimes recycled the number after re-releases; verify via mirror.

title: EIA/TIA IS-553 — Mobile Station-Land Station Compatibility Specification (AMPS)
author: EIA/TIA (Electronic Industries Alliance / Telecommunications Industry Association)
note: Authoritative spec for AMPS control-channel signaling: FOCC / RECC Manchester encoding at 10 kbps, SAT tones (5970/6000/6030 Hz), signaling tone (10 kHz), MIN encoding.

title: War-dial banner fingerprints (aggregate community folklore)
author: aggregate — Phrack 16 (BBS lists), Phrack 18.3 (Packet Switched Networks, Epsilon), Phrack 42.4 (PSN Security, Goggans), Phrack 43.16 (5ESS Guide), Phrack 44.19 (SL-1), ToneLoc/THC-Scan/PhoneSweep result-classification manuals
publication: Distributed across Phrack issues 1985-1998 and scanner-tool documentation
note: The set of 'if a war-dialer hit shows banner X, it is system Y' mappings that circulated in the phreak scene from the mid-1980s onward. No single canonical source; assembled from operator experience across dozens of scans.

title: ANSI T1.113 — Signalling System No. 7 (SS7) ISDN User Part
author: ANSI T1 Committee
note: North American ISUP profile; the '1988' date is when ANSI SS7 was standardized. Companion to ITU Q.767 for international interworking.

title: ANSI T1.403 — Network and Customer Installation Interfaces — DS1 Metallic Interface
author: ANSI T1 Committee
note: The DS1 (T-carrier / T1) spec: 1.544 Mbps, 24 DS0 x 64 kbps + 8 kbps framing. Robbed-bit signaling steals the LSB of every 6th frame per channel for CAS (Channel-Associated Signaling), yielding 56 kbps clear data per DS0.

title: Bellcore GR-506-CORE — LSSGR: Signaling for Analog Interfaces (E&M types)
author: Bellcore / Telcordia
note: Documents E&M types I-V trunk-signaling arrangements: DC E-lead / M-lead states across the interface with battery/ground/loop options.

title: CCITT / ITU-T Q.700 series — Specifications of Signalling System No. 7
author: CCITT / ITU-T
publication: CCITT Q.700 series (1988 Blue Book; ITU-T revisions through Q.700 series 1993+)
note: The SS7 protocol stack: Q.700 overview, Q.701-Q.709 MTP, Q.711-Q.716 SCCP, Q.721-Q.725 TUP, Q.761-Q.766 ISUP, Q.771-Q.775 TCAP, Q.781-Q.782 test specs.

title: CCITT Q.140/Q.180 — Signalling System No. 6 (CCIS)
author: CCITT
note: CCIS = Common Channel Interoffice Signalling. The out-of-band predecessor to SS7. Deployed by AT&T on major routes starting 1976; the transition from CCIS to No.7 (SS7) began 1980 and completed on interoffice trunks by ~1992.

title: Bellcore GR-303-CORE — Integrated Digital Loop Carrier System Generic Requirements
author: Bellcore / Telcordia
note: SLC (Subscriber Loop Carrier) generic requirements. Governed how digital SLC-96 / SLC-2000 terminals interworked with the CO switch — relevant because SLC concentrated subscribers onto a T1 back to the CO, changing what signaling the phreak's local loop actually spoke.

title: The Fortress Phone and Coin Toll Service (Bell Labs Record + Bellcore Technical Publication series)
author: Bell Labs / Bellcore
publication: Bell Labs Record, various issues 1970-1985; Bellcore Technical Publication SR-TSV-000318 (Coin Telephone Signaling)
note: Describes the 1C/1D single-slot ('fortress') payphone hardware and the ACTS coin-supervision protocol. Companion documentation to GR-506-CORE.

title: Nortel Millennium Payphone Reference Manual
author: Northern Telecom
publication: Northern Telecom Millennium Payphone documentation set (1990s)
note: Vendor documentation for the Millennium 'smart' payphone: local coin validation via optical/mass sensor, DTMF/DSP-generated ACTS-look-alike tones for backward compatibility, modem-based management link back to a central Millennium Manager server.

title: COCOT Frequencies and Info
author: community (Phrack 48)
note: COCOT service-mode entry (dial the phone's own number + 4-digit password) and default passwords for Elcotel, Protel, Intellicall boards. Companion piece: 2600 Magazine Spring 1994 'The COCOT Files'.

title: ITU-T O-series (transmission measuring equipment)
author: ITU-T
note: Test-tone and level-measurement practice; the 1004/1020 Hz reference tone family.
